body.x: Midbar Co., Ltd. (CEO Moses Seo) announced its participation in CES 2025, which will occur from January 7 to 10 in Las Vegas. The company will showcase its innovative AirFarm module at the K-Startup Pavilion, emphasizing its potential to revolutionize agriculture in resource-scarce environments.

Midbar aims to transform conventional agriculture by introducing systems that enable sustainable crop production in harsh conditions while significantly reducing essential resource consumption. Using an aeroponic misting system, Midbar has reduced water usage and incorporated vision AI, environmental data, and crop growth analytics to automate production and support data-driven decision-making.

At CES 2024, the inflatable AirFarm module received the Best Innovation and Innovation Awards in the Human Security category. This year, Midbar will introduce a more compact version of the AirFarm, optimized for resource efficiency, earning the company yet another Innovation Award in the Food & AgTech category at CES 2025.

Midbar has successfully entered the Middle East market, leveraging its technological innovations and providing AirFarm solutions to governments and educational institutions in Abu Dhabi, Dubai, and Jordan. The company has partnered with Abu Dhabi University and RBK Holding to supply the AirFarm in Abu Dhabi. It has implemented its solutions and smart agriculture diploma courses at Al al-Bayt University and Jordan University of Science and Technology.

In South Korea, Midbar extends its AirFarm offerings beyond sales by supplying high-quality vegetables grown in its modules to F&B companies as ingredients for health supplements and various foods. The company also collaborates with Dongbang Transport Logistics Co., Ltd. on a carbon footprint reduction project using the AirFarm.

body.cap: Interior of AirFarm │ Photo provided by Midbar

body.x: At CES 2025, Midbar plans to highlight the versatility of its compact AirFarm. Lightweight and durable, the module can be flat-packed for easy transportation and installation. Full setup and cultivation readiness are achievable within half a day.

The AirFarm has an advanced aeroponic system and vapor recycling technology, which reduces water and electricity consumption by 90–95%, maximizing resource efficiency. The module also integrates real-time vision AI, growth, and environmental data to automate cultivation and enable data-driven decision-making.

Midbar shared plans to introduce a new version of the AirFarm in 2025, featuring circular misting technology and nano-climate control systems. These advancements will enable the operation of large-scale, cost-effective plant factories. The company anticipates expanding its reach in Jordan by 2025 and exploring new opportunities in Palestine.
